the convection is not observed in the considered porous media under hydrostatic pressures up to 100 MPa.
the heat transfer in fine-grained fluid-saturated rocks under hydrostatic conditions is always by conduction.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat transfer in fine-grained rocks is due to conduction, while the convective transfer is not possible in the range of pressures and pore sizes considered in this work.
in the considered range of parameters the convection in fluid-saturated rocks does not occur, and the heat transfer in such rocks is due to molecular thermal conductivity.
in fine-grained fluid-saturated rocks under high pressures, convection does not occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convective transfer of heat in rocks is not possible in most cases, except for rocks with a very large porosity.
the convective heat transfer is possible only under conditions where the Rayleigh filtration numbers are greater than unity.
the convective heat transfer is not possible in compact rocks with a low degree of porosity, which are the most common in the Earth's interior.
